newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission launches youth volunteer programme.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission launches youth volunteer programme.

text.p: Young people in the European Union will have a chance to travel to foreign countries for voluntary work stints lasting several months under a plan agreed on Wednesday by the European Commission.
The voluntary programme, to run from 1998 to 2002 with a budget of 60 million European currency units ($74 million) for the first two years, is aimed at people aged between 18 and 25.
Volunteers will be able to join a wide range of programmes, mainly within the European Union and but also further afield in central and eastern Europe, Africa and the Carribean.
The EU executive agreed to fund participants' travel and a monthly allowance of 200 Ecus but expects voluntary organisations running projects to pay for bed and board.

It said a 1996 pilot project, involving 2,500 people from the 15-country EU and covering projects ranging from historic site restoration in Germany to a Spanish "meals-on-wheels" cooked-food-delivery service to the old, had paved the way for the full-blown programme announced on Wednesday.

"Whether we are talking about learning support for disadvantaged children, the regeneration of run-down areas, the cleaning up of a natural site or assisting the disabled, such activities are enriching in more than one way," European Youth Commissioner Edith Cresson told a news conference.

Cresson said periods on the programme would not count towards any EU country's military service requirements, unless governments so decided, and added that it should not be seen as a ruse to pull people off unemployment benefit.

"European voluntary service is not just another trick to reduce unemployment statistics. The activities it proposes are in no way a substitute for potential or esxisting jobs," the accompanying statement said.
Cresson said that the plan should not be elitist and should encourage disadvantaged young people also to get a look in. ($=0.81 Ecu)
